scores.claim_text: Axon's customer base is expanding beyond law enforcement to include attorneys, corrections, fire and emergency medical services personnel and the U.S. military.
scores.M_value: NOT_FOUND (J-Book corpus) | usaspending: 15 DoD awards, $3.4M total (cumulative since 2020)
scores.interpretation: AXON does not name any specific Pentagon Program Element, PE number, or DoD program-of-record on which forward revenue depends. The claim is qualitative customer-segment language ('U.S. military' as one of many expanding customer types). The U.S. military DoD obligations are real but tiny ($3.4M cumulative — body cameras, TASERs, license renewals, including a small $250K Dedrone-related JCO demo prize). They are immaterial against $1.6B FY2023 revenue (~0.07% annualized). No forward J-Book exposure to verify because there is no PE-tied claim to test. PASS on the J-Book divergence pattern — the company is NOT making a J-Book-load-bearing claim, so there is no divergence to catch.

scores.claim_text: Axon's indoor tactical drone hardware platform, Sky-Hero, competes with Brinc, Indoor Robotics and XTEND in the indoor tactical drone market.
scores.M_check: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(program_name='Short Range Reconnaissance Program of Record') | pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(contractor_name='Sky-Hero') | usaspending(Sky-Hero)
scores.M_value: J-Book SRR: NOT_FOUND | J-Book Sky-Hero contractor: NOT_FOUND | usaspending Sky-Hero: 0 DoD awards
scores.interpretation: Sky-Hero is positioned as a LAW-ENFORCEMENT tactical drone (interior breach reconnaissance for SWAT/tactical teams), NOT a DoD Program of Record contender. The named comparables (Brinc, XTEND) are also law-enforcement / IDF subjects, not DoD primes. Although Short Range Reconnaissance (SRR) is a real Army PoR, AXON makes no claim to be in SRR — the Skydio / Teal / Anduril cohort owns that PoR. UNVERIFIABLE for the J-Book pattern: company does not name a DoD program; corpus does not cover law-enforcement tactical drone procurement. Coverage gap, not a red flag.

scores.claim_text: Axon entered into a definitive agreement on April 30, 2024 to acquire the remaining outstanding stock of Dedrone Holdings, Inc. for ~$400.0M; Dedrone is described as a market leader in airspace security / counter-UAS.
scores.M_value: J-Book C-sUAS / C-UAS: NOT_FOUND (corpus does not cover JCO C-sUAS line items — coverage gap) | usaspending Dedrone: 5 DoD awards, $270.7K cumulative (mostly $19K-$110K Dedrone Defender V3 / annual license SKUs at AF Sustainment / NAVAIR test orgs) | acq_coherence: 0.25 LOW_COHERENCE, flagged is_revenue_synthetic=True
scores.interpretation: Dedrone is the only acquisition that materially diversifies AXON away from its police-only thesis into the DoD/critical-infrastructure stack. Pre-acquisition Dedrone DoD revenue is trivially small ($270K cumulative — orders of magnitude below what would justify a $400M valuation if DoD were the primary buyer). The thesis 'market leader in airspace security' is reasonable for the commercial / critical-infrastructure C-UAS market (stadiums, prisons, airports) but does NOT translate to a DoD program-of-record revenue stream. acq_coherence flags Dedrone as low_coherence + revenue_synthetic relative to AXON's police thesis — i.e., a $400M rollup into an adjacent vertical where the operational case for synergy with TASERs / body cameras is thin. This is the closest the J-Book pattern comes to firing on AXON: not a 'PE got zeroed' signal (no claimed PE), but a 'expensive diversification into a market whose DoD obligations are 1/1000th of the headline narrative' signal. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY of the implied DoD-adjacency thesis.

scores.claim_text: As of December 31, 2023, Axon had approximately $7.1 billion of future contracted revenue.
scores.M_value: usaspending DoD: 15 awards, $3.4M cumulative — i.e., DoD is <0.05% of $7.1B RPO | J-Book: NOT_FOUND
scores.interpretation: The $7.1B RPO is overwhelmingly state/local police subscription bundles (TASER 10 5-year installments + Axon Body 4 + Evidence.com SaaS + Axon Fleet + Axon Cloud). DoD is not a material share of contracted revenue. Therefore there is no Pentagon J-Book line item whose status would meaningfully impair the $7.1B RPO. PASS — the contracted revenue is structurally insulated from Pentagon budget cycle risk, by virtue of customer-base composition.
